newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-W. Australia says undecided on gold royalty.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-W. Australia says undecided on gold royalty.

text.p: The Western Australian state government has made no decision so far on whether to impose a gold royalty levy on the state's mining industry, premier Richard Court said on Wednesday.
"At this stage no decision has been made as to a gold royalty," Court told a gold industry conference.
Court said the idea of a royalty was "a perennial issue" for the state.
He said any decision to introduce a royalty would only be made after consultation with the state's mining sector.
The prospect of a royalty follows a cut in annual Federal grants to Western Australia of about A$33.5 million.
"We have a difficult budget," Court said.
Gold miners in the state believe that a royalty could make some mines uneconomic.
Peter Lalor, the managing director of Sons of Gwalia Ltd, said there was "industry disquiet" about the possibility of a royalty being introduced.
The state accounts for about 70 percent of the nation's total annual gold production and the mining sector has estimated that a royalty of about two percent would raise about A$70 million.
The government has not mentioned a specific royalty figure.
The gold mining industry pays normal Federal corporate profits tax but in Western Australia has long been exempt from the type of state royalty imposed on other minerals.
